Building a time-series model means the same steps every time, and much
of the effort goes into turning their output into a document. `dazflow`
runs the steps from configuration and renders every result in one house
style. This page follows one project, made by the command line, through
the main ideas.

```sh
pip install dazflow
dazflow init my-model
```

```python
import dazflow as dz

project = dz.project.load("my-model")
```

## Steps

Each step is one call that takes data and its configuration, and a later
step takes the earlier one's result as an argument instead of importing
it. `project.run()` runs the pipeline in memory and writes nothing;
`project.write(run)` writes the datasets, the reports and the run record.

```python
run = project.run()                 # ingest, clean, explore, build, select,
                                    # forecast, diagnose, report
ds = run.results["clean"].dataset   # the series in levels
ex = dz.explore.run(ds, project.step_config("explore"))
cand = dz.build.run(ds, project.step_config("build"), explore=ex)
sel = dz.select.run(ds.with_scenarios(scenarios, severity), build=cand)
sel.chosen, sel.decision            # proposed by the default rule until confirmed
record = project.write(run)         # reports/<step>/, reports/document/, reports/record.json
```

## Report and replay

The report is built from the run record alone: a Word document with a
contents list, a summary, every step's section in pipeline order and a
configuration appendix, and a replay script beside it.

```python
doc = dz.report.run(record)
doc.sections                        # Contents, Summary, one per step, two appendices
```

A replay reruns every step from the record and compares every recorded
number with what it computes now: floats within a relative 1e-9, the rest
exactly.

```python
replay = project.replay()
replay.passed, replay.differences   # each difference: its path and both values
```

## Gates and findings

Every step ends in checks against configured thresholds. A failed gate
is reported, never hidden, and is overridden only with a reason written
in configuration.

```python
ex.gate.passed
ex.finding.text
```

## Artefacts

Tables and figures carry stable identifiers and are ready for a Word
document.

```python
dz.render.write(ex.artefacts["T3.3"], "screen.docx")
```

The same project runs from the command line:

```sh
dazflow run --to select
dazflow run --from forecast
dazflow report                      # reports/document/document.docx
dazflow replay                      # exit 0 when the run reproduces its record
python reports/document/replay.py   # the same, without the command line
```

## Your own components

A model form, check or transform is registered once and then named in
configuration like a built-in one.

```python
class ThetaConfig(dz.Config):
    theta: float = 2.0

@dz.models.register("theta")
class Theta(dz.models.ModelForm):
    Config = ThetaConfig

    def _fit(self, y, X, spec) -> dz.models.FittedModel:
        ...
```

A form passes the same contract as the built-in ones:

```python
from dazflow.testing import ModelContract

class TestTheta(ModelContract):
    key = "theta"
```

Any form, built-in or not, can be scored out of sample by refitting it at
successive origins:

```python
y, X = ...   # the target and its drivers, on a PeriodIndex
ev = dz.evaluation.evaluate(
    dz.models.get("ols")(), y, X,
    splitter=dz.evaluation.Expanding(initial=40, horizon=4),
)
ev.score("mase"), ev.score("coverage")
```

```yaml
# my-model/config/build.yaml
forms: [ols, arimax, theta]
```
